vocabulary.definition: In this sense, "random" is just a way to describe "nothing specific". I used to date a bunch of random girls before I met my wife. I love movies. Just give me a bunch of random DVDs and I'll watch all of them.
A "Wiki" is an Internet term that talks about content that can be added to and edited by the users in an online community
If something is "pre existing" it means that it was around before. It existed before. In the case of the dialog, a "pre existing" article is an article that was already written.
In this sense, the "accuracy" of the content is talking about how true it is. I wouldn't read those statistics. They look interesting but I don't think they are very accurate.

Financial compensation is talking about the getting money for your work. Wikipedia gets compensated by donations. Google's financial compensation comes in the form of advertisements. That is why the service is free to users.

If you can "count on" someone or something it means you can rely on it or trust it. The person who wrote that article doesn't know what he's talking about. I wouldn't count on the information or opinions.

If someone is "accountable" for something it means you can hold them responsible for something. If it's proven that the patient died because of a doctor error, then the doctor will be held accountable and lose his license and get sued millions.
